open_questions: Serverless release notes never state an Apache Spark version; each server version only 'roughly corresponds' to a Databricks Runtime version, recorded as spark_from (the DBR's Spark version is on the classic runtime list). Serverless version 16.1 corresponds to both DBR 16.0 and 16.1 (both Apache Spark 3.5.0); spark_from names dbr-16.1.

The weekly releases since July 6, 2026 say they 'include updates from Databricks Runtime 18' (July 6) or 'Databricks Runtime 19' (August 17 onward) rather than naming a corresponding DBR; the matrix reads that as tracking DBR 18 LTS and DBR 19, and serverless-specific claims override what they inherit.

Environment versions state a Databricks Connect client version but no Spark version; spark_from follows that Connect version to its DBR via the Connect requirements page ('Databricks Connect version numbers correspond to Databricks Runtime version numbers'). The per-version pages list newer Connect patch releases than the index (e.g. version 1: 14.3.23 vs 14.3.7), and the version 4 page says only 'Databricks Connect: 17' while the index says 17.3.2; the index value is used for version 4. Connect 18 (environment version 5) maps to Databricks Runtime 18 (dbr-18lts).

Serverless compute always runs the most recently released version, so superseded server versions have no stated status; only the current releases (which include updates from DBR 19) are marked current.
The environment version index lists no end-of-support version; all six are within their three-year support window.

Iceberg on serverless notebooks and jobs: the Iceberg page requires serverless compute for managed-table maintenance and names Databricks Runtime and Databricks SQL as authoring surfaces, but does not state serverless notebook/job support; no claim added.

This allows Databricks to upgrade the server independently, delivering performance improvements, security enhancements, and bug fixes without requiring any code changes to workloads.

platforms.name: IBM Analytics Engine (serverless)
open_questions: Release notes (Dec 2025): 'In IBM Analytics Engine, Apache Spark 3.5.4 and Apache Spark 4.0 are the supported versions.' The Spark 4.0 patch version is not stated.
Spark 3.4 (3.4.4 per Feb 2025 notes) is no longer named as supported after Dec 2025, but no deprecation notice for 3.4 was found; omitted.
The provisioning page (lastupdated 2023-10-10) is stale: it still says 'Spark 3.4. is the default version' and lists 3.3.2 as 'Removed(Not Supported)'.

Sources are IBM's public docs source repo on GitHub (ibm-cloud-docs/AnalyticsEngine), which renders at cloud.ibm.com/docs/AnalyticsEngine; 'in IBM Analytics Engine' brand placeholders appear as keyrefs in the raw source.

claims.note: The service is deprecated: no new instances from May 8, 2026 and end of support April 8, 2027; IBM points to the watsonx.data Spark engine.
claims.quote: The IBM Analytics Engine is now deprecated. No new instances can be created or purchased starting on May 8, 2026. The service will no longer be supported by IBM Cloud as of April 8, 2027.

platforms.name: Alibaba Cloud EMR Serverless Spark
open_questions: The engine version page (last updated Jul 08, 2026) gives no per-version status or end-of-support; every listed engine is recorded as 'supported' and the newest (esr-5.3.0) as 'current'.
Release dates are taken from the release-note pages that first list an engine (2025-11-12, 2026-01-26, 2026-04-15); dates for esr-5.3.0, esr-4.9.x, esr-3.8.0 and older engines were not found.
esr-2.x engines (Spark 3.3.1) are listed back to esr-2.1; only esr-2.9.0 is included here.
Which engine versions support Fusion, and Python versions per engine, are not stated on the engine version page.

claims.note: Fusion is a built-in vectorized SQL engine, enabled per session; it does not accelerate RDD jobs or UDFs and only partially supports ORC.
claims.quote: The Fusion engine is a vectorized SQL execution engine built into EMR Serverless Spark. ... Enable it by turning on the Use Fusion Acceleration switch when creating a session. ... The Fusion engine does not accelerate the following job types: Resilient Distributed Dataset (RDD) jobs Jobs that use user-defined functions (UDFs)
